aiOverview.content: Friday the 13th is a widely recognized day of superstition in Western culture, occurring when the 13th day of a month falls on a Friday. Considered unlucky, it stems from beliefs surrounding the number 13 (triskaidekaphobia) and Friday biblical references. It is also a famous 1980 horror film franchise featuring Jason Voorhees, known for popularizing the slasher genre. Origins and Superstition The Number 13: Considered unlucky, sometimes linked to 13 people at the Last Supper or Loki being the 13th guest at a Norse feast, according to History.com. Friday: Historically associated with unlucky events, including the crucifixion of Jesus. Paraskevidekatriaphobia: The term for a fear of Friday the 13th. Frequency: It occurs at least once every year, but can occur up to three times in a single year, such as in 2026, notes Scientific American and The New York Times. Film Franchise Original 1980 Film: Directed by Sean S. Cunningham, it focused on camp counselors at Camp Crystal Lake. Jason Voorhees: While the first film featured his mother, the iconic hockey-masked killer Jason became the primary antagonist in subsequent sequels, says IMDb and IMDb. Impact: The series is a staple of horror cinema, known for its, gory effects and high commercial success, notes IMDb. Cultural Significance Tattoo Tradition: Many tattoo shops offer special "$13" themed flash deals on these days, as seen in the Reno Gazette Journal. 2026 Dates: In 2026, Friday the 13th occurs in February, March, and November, reports USA Today.
